audit.title: VRF Best Practices

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Sections open with the intent-answer pattern: "If you need to generate a random number within a given range, use modulo…". Weak spot: the page intro is filler ("These are example best practices…") rather than a liftable definition of what VRF best practices cover.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong: 5 headings, clean H1→H2, 0 level skips, 0 sections over 600 words (max 418). No tables, but the content is procedural, so their absence is minor.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Code carries real values (coordinator `0x9Ddf…`, keyHash, `callbackGasLimit = 100000`, `requestConfirmations = 3`), but prose has only 4 numerals and 0 with units. State limits like `MAX_NUM_WORDS` numerically in prose, not just a code comment.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 4 links, 1 to a primary source (Solidity docs). Under-linked: no inline link to VRF concepts, subscription funding, or supported-networks page from the prose where those terms first appear.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Weakest content dimension. The page never crisply defines its own terms (e.g. what `numWords`, `requestId`, or a "gas lane" is) in a liftable sentence near first use.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, no og/twitter tags. Head metadata could not be captured here, so verify server-side — but the measured absence of schema and dates is a real gap for E-E-A-T and freshness signals.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: The final multi-path contract is complete (SPDX, pragma, imports, constructor, addresses) and well-labeled. But 3 of 4 blocks show no imports and one uses placeholder comments; an agent lifting the "simultaneous requests" snippet gets no imports or contract scaffold.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Headings match "how do I get a random number in a range / multiple values / concurrent requests." Missing: a troubleshooting/FAQ segment and error-string coverage (e.g. callback out-of-gas, `numWords` exceeding max).

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Clear, consistent naming (`requestId`, `fulfillRandomWords`, VRF v2.5). No action needed.

audit.summary: This is a task-oriented VRF v2.5 best-practices page: four concrete patterns (range, multiple values, concurrent requests, branching execution) each headed by a how-to statement and backed by Solidity. Its biggest strength is clean, well-sized chunks with action-phrased headings that map to real developer intents. Its biggest opportunity is machine-readability — no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, no visible last-updated — compounded by thin prose specifics and code snippets stripped of imports. Solid, retrievable content that under-signals trust and freshness to engines.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD + canonical + last-updated
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `about: "Chainlink VRF"`, a self-canonical URL, and render a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Freshness and schema are the E-E-A-T signals engines use to trust and rank a source; all are currently absent.

recommendations.title: Add a troubleshooting / FAQ section with error-phrased headings
recommendations.issue: No symptom or error-string coverage; devs query "fulfillRandomWords not called" or "numWords exceeds max."
recommendations.change: Add short Q-headings like "Why does my VRF callback run out of gas?" and "Error: numWords exceeds MAX_NUM_WORDS" with one-line answers.
recommendations.why: Symptom-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses, even when the fix is elsewhere on the page.

recommendations.title: Complete the standalone snippets
recommendations.issue: 3 of 4 blocks show no imports; agents can't compile the mapping snippets in isolation.
recommendations.change: Add the imports/contract wrapper (or a one-line "add to the VRFConsumerBaseV2Plus contract above" note) so each block is self-contained.
recommendations.why: Copy-pasteable, complete code raises agent-runnability and citation likelihood.

recommendations.title: Surface numeric limits and defaults in prose
recommendations.issue: `MAX_NUM_WORDS` and default `requestConfirmations = 3` live only in code comments.
recommendations.change: State in prose: "`numWords` cannot exceed `MAX_NUM_WORDS` (500); `requestConfirmations` defaults to 3, min 3."
recommendations.why: Quantitative claims in prose are among the highest-lift extractable facts.

recommendations.title: Add canonical one-line definitions near first use
recommendations.issue: Terms used without a liftable definition.
recommendations.change: e.g. "`keyHash` is the gas lane — the maximum gas price VRF will pay to fulfill your request."
recommendations.why: Crisp verbatim-liftable definitions outperform diffuse explanation.

recommendations.title: Enrich inline citations
recommendations.where: prose mentions of subscriptions, coordinator, supported networks
recommendations.issue: Only 4 links; key concepts unlinked in prose.
recommendations.change: Link "subscription method," "supported networks," and "VRF v2.5" to their canonical docs pages inline at first use.
recommendations.why: Inline authoritative links raise credibility and citation rate.

antiPatterns: Placeholder-comment block (`THIS IS AN EXAMPLE CONTRACT…`) — acceptable as a safety warning, but the same disclaimer generates the flagged unassigned identifiers; keep it but it slightly dilutes liftability.
Vague intro line ("These are example best practices…") — non-liftable filler.
No stale-content risk visible, but this cannot be confirmed without a dateModified.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top of the page — good site-level signal.
Verify whether `TechArticle` schema and canonical/date tags are injected server-side (head metadata was not captured here); the CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a definitive read.
Cross-link from the VRF v2.5 hub and migration pages into this page to reinforce the canonical-hub pattern.
